title: National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2018
official_summary:
National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2018

This bill amends the Earthquake Hazards Reduction Act of 1977 to reauthorize through FY2023, and expand activities under, the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program to include: (1) gathering information on community resilience (i.e., the ability of a community to prepare for, recover from, and adapt to earthquakes); (2) publishing a systematic set of maps of active faults and folds, liquefaction susceptibility, susceptibility for earthquake-induced landslides, and other seismically induced hazards; and (3) continuing the development of the Advanced National Seismic System, including earthquake early warning capabilities.

(Sec. 2) The bill modifies the Act's findings to include Puerto Rico as vulnerable to the hazards of earthquakes, and adds Oregon and Tennessee to the list of states cited as having major or moderate seismic risk.

(Sec. 3) With respect to earthquake hazard reduction activities, the bill revises or expands the duties of: (1) the Interagency Coordinating Committee on Earthquake Hazards Reduction, (2) the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), (3) the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), (4) the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), and (5) the National Science Foundation.

(Sec. 4) The Government Accountability Office shall complete a review of federal earthquake hazard risk reduction efforts.

(Sec. 5) NIST and FEMA must jointly convene a committee of experts to assess and recommend options for improving seismic safety standards.

(Sec. 6) The USGS must submit to Congress a five-year management plan for the continued operation of the Advanced National Seismic System.

summary.headline: This law extends and expands the federal earthquake hazards reduction program through fiscal year 2023 and adds new mapping, resilience, and early-warning work.
summary.what_it_does: The law reauthorizes the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program through fiscal year 2023 and widens its scope. It asks agencies to collect information on how communities prepare for and recover from earthquakes, publish detailed hazard maps, and keep developing the Advanced National Seismic System, including earthquake early warning. It also updates the program's findings to name Puerto Rico, Oregon, and Tennessee as areas with seismic risk, revises duties for NIST, FEMA, USGS, and the National Science Foundation, and requires a GAO review, an expert committee on seismic safety standards, and a USGS five-year management plan for the seismic system.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of earthquake-prone areas, including Puerto Rico, Oregon, and Tennessee
who_it_affects.how: Federal earthquake hazard maps and early warning work are expected to expand, and these areas are now named in the law as facing seismic risk.

who_it_affects.group: Local emergency managers and community planners
who_it_affects.how: FEMA and other agencies are directed to gather information on community resilience that may inform local preparedness and recovery planning.

who_it_affects.group: Engineers, builders, and building code officials
who_it_affects.how: A federal expert committee will assess and recommend options for improving seismic safety standards.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies such as NIST, FEMA, USGS, and the National Science Foundation
who_it_affects.how: Each agency has revised or added earthquake-related duties under the program.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 11, 2018; the program authorization runs through fiscal year 2023.
